facts.c: Hundi (sending money through unlicensed private agents outside the banking system) is illegal in Bangladesh
facts.q: Despite its illegality, the system thrives in parallel with formal financial institutions

facts.c: Hundi brokers deliver money to the family's doorstep and in 2022-2024 offered a better taka rate than banks (for example Tk 115 against about Tk 108 per dollar)
facts.q: While formal channels provide an exchange rate of around Tk108 per dollar, hundi offers rates as high as Tk115.

facts.c: Undocumented workers abroad cannot use formal channels and often have no way to send money but hundi
facts.q: many workers are undocumented, so there is no way for them to send money via any formal channel

facts.c: Hundi brokers settle transactions through mobile-money (MFS) accounts such as bKash and Nagad
facts.q: Brokers use MFS to settle transactions, creating a seamless system that blends informal practices with formal technologies

facts.c: Bangladesh's Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) had suspended or frozen about 55,000 mobile-money accounts linked to online gambling and digital hundi by June 2026
facts.q: Earlier, on 25 June, Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury told parliament that the BFIU had suspended or frozen transactions of around 55,000 MFS accounts linked to online gambling and digital hundi activities.

facts.c: In August 2026 the BFIU decided to freeze about 14,000 more mobile-money accounts over online gambling and digital hundi
facts.q: has decided to freeze around 14,000 more mobile financial service (MFS) accounts over alleged links to online gambling and digital hundi activities

facts.c: Cambodia has no personal income tax as such; employees pay a monthly salary tax
facts.q: Instead, a monthly salary tax is imposed on individuals who derive income from employment.

facts.c: Salary tax for residents, on monthly salary in riel: 0% up to KHR 1,500,000; 5% to 2,000,000; 10% to 8,500,000; 15% to 12,500,000; 20% above
Non-residents pay salary tax at a flat 20%, as a final tax
facts.q: Non-residents are taxed at a flat rate of 20%, which constitutes a final tax.

facts.c: Fringe benefits are taxed at a flat 20% of the amount paid
facts.q: Fringe benefits are taxable at the flat rate of 20% of the amount paid.

facts.c: A tax resident is someone domiciled or with a principal home in Cambodia, or present more than 182 days in a 12-month period
facts.q: present in Cambodia for more than 182 days in a 12-month period

facts.c: The employer deducts salary tax each month (pay-as-you-earn) and pays it to the tax authorities within 20 days after the month; employees file no annual return
facts.q: Employers must deduct salary tax from employees' salaries in accordance with the tax tables on a pay-as-you-earn (PAYE) basis.
facts.note: Same page: 'no later than 20 days after the end of the month'; 'Employees do not have to file an annual return.'

facts.c: A deduction of KHR 150,000 a month is allowed for each dependent child or spouse
facts.q: A deduction of KHR 150,000 per month is allowed for each dependent child or spouse.

facts.c: Law on Foreign Exchange (1997), Article 13: a traveller carrying means of payment of USD 10,000 or more (or the riel equivalent), in or out, must declare it to customs at the border
facts.q: The export or import of the means of payment equaling or exceeding ten thousand US dollars (USD 10,000) in foreign exchange or the equivalent amount in domestic currency by a traveler shall be declared to the customs officers at border crossings

facts.c: Law on Foreign Exchange, Article 22: failing to declare under Article 13 is fined 10% of the amount
facts.q: Any person who violates Article 11 or paragraph 1 of Article 13 of the present law shall be liable for a fine of ten per cent (10%) of the amount involved.

facts.c: Law on Foreign Exchange, Article 13: taking out cash above the limit set by the National Bank needs the National Bank's prior examination
facts.q: The export of cash in excess of the limit set by the regulation of the Central Bank shall be subject to prior examination by the Central Bank.

facts.c: Law on Foreign Exchange, Article 12: import or export of raw gold or precious stones is free but must be declared to the National Bank in advance if a transaction is worth USD 10,000 or more
facts.q: shall be subject to prior declaration to the Central Bank if the value of each transaction equals or exceeds ten thousand US dollars (USD 10,000).

facts.c: Cambodian customs: bringing in foreign currency is not limited, but sums over USD 10,000 must be declared
facts.q: Import of foreign currencies to Cambodia is not limited, although declaration is required for the sums of over US$10,000.00 (ten thousand US dollars)
facts.note: Law on Foreign Exchange Art. 13 (G-fact on odm-kh-law-on-foreign-exchange-1997) says 'equaling or exceeding' USD 10,000; airport page says 'over'.

facts.c: Cambodian customs: taking out more than USD 10,000 in foreign currency without an entry declaration needs a National Bank of Cambodia permit and customs approval
facts.q: Foreign currency in the amount exceeding US$10,000.00 (ten thousand US dollars) is required to obtain the permit from the National Bank of Cambodia and approval before an exportation from the General Department of Customs and Excise, should there be no import declaration of the currency at their entry.

facts.c: Cambodian customs: all arriving passengers fill in the Passenger's Declaration Form and hand it to customs before leaving the arrival terminal
facts.q: All passengers are obliged to fill out the Passenger's Declaration Form and submit it to Customs before leaving the arrival terminal.

facts.c: Cambodian customs duty-free allowance on arrival: up to 2 litres of alcohol, 200 cigarettes, 350 ml perfume, and personal belongings and devices needed for travel; goods worth USD 100 or more pay duty
facts.q: Goods worth the equivalent to or greater than US$100 shall be subjected to pay customs duties and taxes.
facts.note: Same page: 'Any type of alcohol no more than 2 liters'; 'Not exceeding 200 cigarettes'; 'Perfume and cosmetics not exceeding 350 milliliters'; 'An appropriate number of belongings and devices needed for traveling that are not prohibited.'

facts.c: Cambodian customs: drug trafficking can be punished with life imprisonment
facts.q: A passenger who is convicted of this offense can receive life imprisonment in accordance with the laws of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

facts.c: Bangladesh customs: any amount of foreign currency may be brought in, but more than USD 10,000 or its equivalent must be declared on the FMJ form
facts.q: if more than USD 10,000 or an equivalent amount of foreign currency is brought from abroad, the FMJ form must be filled out and declared at customs

facts.c: Bangladesh customs: a passenger can bring 2 used mobile phones and 1 new mobile phone once a year without duty and tax
facts.q: A passenger can import 2 (two) used mobile phones and 1 (one) new mobile phone only once per year without paying duty and tax

facts.c: Bangladesh customs: a passenger may bring at most 117 g (10 tola) of gold, as one bar, once a year, declared and paying Tk 5,000 per 11.664 g (about Tk 50,000 for 117 g)
facts.q: A passenger can carry a maximum of 117 grams or 1 (one) gold bar worth 10 tola only once per year after declaring it at the customs.
facts.note: Same page: 'Customs tax on every 11.664 grams of gold = 5,000/- Taka'; 'Customs tax on every 117 grams of gold = 50,000/- Taka (approximate)'.

facts.c: Bangladesh customs: undeclared gold leads to detention, arrest and a criminal case; gold above 117 g is confiscated
facts.q: Passengers carrying undeclared gold will be detained, arrested and a criminal case will be filed and handed over to the nearest police station.

facts.c: Bangladesh customs: a passenger can bring one item duty-free from a list that includes a laptop, and 100 g of gold and 200 g of silver ornaments (no more than 12 of one type)
facts.q: 1 (one) hundred gram gold ornaments and 2 (two) hundred gram silver ornaments (not more than 12 of the same type of ornaments)

facts.c: Bangladesh customs: no Bangladeshi passport holder may bring alcohol
facts.q: No Bangladeshi passport holder can carry alcoholic beverages.

facts.c: Wage Earner Development Bond: a 5-year Bangladesh government bond for legal wage earners, sold at authorised-dealer bank branches in Bangladesh and at Bangladeshi banks' branches and exchange houses abroad, from Tk 25,000 to Tk 50 lakh, with no purchase limit
facts.q: বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক দেশে অবস্থিত যে কোন তফশিলী ব্যাংকের অথরাইজড ডিলার (AD) শাখা এবং বিদেশে অবস্থিত বাংলাদেশের তফসিলী ব্যাংকের শাখা, এক্সচেঞ্জ হাউস, এক্সচেঞ্জ কোম্পানি হতে ক্রয় করা যায়।
facts.note: Same page: denominations Tk 25,000 to Tk 50,00,000; term 5 years; 'ক্রয়ের ঊর্ধ্বসীমা: কোন ঊর্ধ্বসীমা নেই' (no upper limit).

facts.c: Wage Earner Development Bond pays 12% simple profit on maturity (top rate)
A 2025 study cited by Cambodian unions and NGOs found garment workers' average monthly take-home pay was USD 287 against median household spending of USD 391
facts.q: a 2025 study found average monthly take-home earnings of $287 compared with median household spending of $391

facts.c: A Phnom Penh garment worker said that after rent, utilities and food little is left, and she needs overtime to reach about USD 320 a month including transport, housing and food allowances
facts.q: Nita said she would need to work overtime to bring her monthly income to about $320, including transport, accommodation and food allowances.
